source_binding: Final Go checks match committed Go source. The prose check matches the committed document. Each command retains exact dirty inputs, source snapshots, output, timestamps, and terminal exit status.
qualification: Local legacy relocation recovery. CSP5 remains incomplete. No mapped task acceptance, native Linux/Windows execution, PR, merge, or released-pair credit.
previous_goal_turn: No progress: the previous turn only revalidated CSP4 completion. This continuation implements and verifies durable legacy relocation recovery.
limits: The original process-exit regression failed after relocation, before workspace publication, and after workspace installation. Four failed events include their parent.

Version 4 preparation journals bind both parent identities, store metadata, every retained generation, the optional Windows lock alias, and the projected workspace inventory. Complete receipts flush before relocation and workspace publication.

Explicit migration retry validates the recorded store and workspace, restores the store without replacing another destination, retires owned staging, and retries migration. Ordinary projection and repair refuse pending relocation.

Recovery preserves changed files and identities, unknown entries, incomplete receipts, wrong destinations, and active writers. It permits remaining owned workspace entries after interrupted rollback and accepts an already restored store.

Windows recovery reuses its recorded hard-link alias. An absent alias can be recreated only for the recorded commit-lock identity. Cleanup releases the lock and checks the original alias identity, content, and access.

Actual process exits cover complete inventory before relocation, moved store, prepared candidate, installed workspace, and completed projection. Partial rollback tests separately simulate an incomplete workspace cleanup or an already restored store.

Additional checks cover fourteen changed-state cases, workspace and commit writers, canceled recovery, bounded parent scans, alias absence and changes, older journal rejection, and publication after an equivalent-JSON journal edit.

Generation enumeration uses batches of 128 entries. Existing 32 MiB, 120000-event journal limits and per-tree inventory limits apply before relocation. The parent scan stops at 4096 entries before cleanup.

The first integration attempt did not compile because a version-compatibility test lacked its fmt import. A broader run exposed changed error classification for a replaced store. Both failures remain archived with their corrections.
The first prose check found one seven-sentence paragraph. Its final split preserves the text and passes the repository prose check.
Go policy and Linux/Windows AMD64 compilation pass. Compilation does not qualify native execution. Test event counts include parents.

A completed migration retires its journal; a repeated completed command reports the existing destination. Crashes with incomplete ownership or an unrecorded empty enclosure remain preserved for explicit recovery.
Evidence and discovery staging, generation retention, history compaction, twelve mapped subcases, full task verification, required review, native CI, and merge remain open.

The first full suite passed 382 test events and failed one writer-identity case. Preparation now reports changed writer identity as a retryable conflict. A separate fail-before test proved open setup handles after cleanup refusal; a deferred release corrects it. Both focused race regressions pass.

All current checks use the observed concurrent goago migration in go.mod and go.sum. Those inputs remain archived and outside the catalog commit. Final task qualification must use the final committed module graph.

The final canonical prose check passes. Its source snapshots retain observed tooling edits separately from the six owned documentation files. Plan maintenance preserves task criteria, invariants, scope, and the goal block.
